evidence: Read the fix delta /tmp/claude-1000/-home-labdrian-labdrian-sdd-overlay/befdc48e-903a-43ab-9251-fddebbec827d/scratchpad/c22t4fix.diff, which touches extract.go, extract_test.go, header.go and sourcefs_test.go.
Read the frozen round-0 ledger: 63254c3398b9-6.polisher.json F1 WARNING and 63254c3398b9-4.json F1-F3 SUGGESTIONs.

Polisher F1 is resolved. At head, extract.go:150 now applies filepath.Clean(origin.URI) after ResolveOrigin (source.go:54-66) and before Reader.Lstat at extract.go:151. Cleaning turns a Path of `link/` or `link/.` back into `link`. Lstat then reports EntrySymlink, and the default branch at extract.go:170-172 refuses it as 'neither file nor directory' (D1). scan therefore never runs on the link. The new real-filesystem test sourcefs_test.go TestExtractRefusesALinkNamedWithATrailingSlash checks both spellings through sourcefs.Reader. Its helpers mkdir, symlink and write exist at sourcefs_test.go:343-357. Not run: I had no shell, so this rests on reading only.

Ids and Source-URIs: the fix does not change any id. canonicalOrigin (header.go:280) already applied filepath.Clean to the URI before SourceID, and an Override is untouched because it lives in its own field (header.go:266-272, sourceURI at extract.go:325-329). The only visible change is that sourceURI(origin) now writes the cleaned path for an absolute Path that was not clean. That now matches the canonical string the id is built from, so the two no longer disagree. A relative Path is unchanged, because filepath.Join in ResolveOrigin already cleaned it.

I checked whether lexical cleaning opens a new escape. For an absolute Path like `/a/link/..`, the operating system would previously have resolved `..` through the link's target. Cleaning now names `/a`, so no link is followed and nothing outside the named path is read. That narrows what can be reached rather than widening it. A link as an intermediate component (`/a/link/x`) behaves as it did at base. The D1 rule covers only a Path that is itself a link, so the fix did not introduce that case.

Traversal guard in scan/walk (extract.go:226-279): the delta does not change it. root is still filepath.Clean of an already-cleaned URI, and the below() and outside_root checks plus the per-entry Lstat are unchanged. No new route lets a run report success while a failure is hidden.

Ledger 4.json F1 is resolved: the Request.Origin comment (extract.go:21-22 in the delta) now says a scan uses neither the Override nor the Title. The scan doc (extract.go:219-225) now names both request-level failures. The stale 'taken before the scan is built' wording in header.go:57-59 now says a scan request with an override is refused (D3).

Ledger 4.json F2 is resolved. The scan doc states that the whole scan is aborted and earlier results dropped. The new test TestExtractRefusesAScanWithAFileOverMaxChunks pins it: listing order is c.png, b.md, a.md and the sort processes a.md first, so a source exists before b.md fails. The test asserts ErrTooManyChunks and an empty Result, matching scan's `return Result{}, err` at extract.go:248-249. ChunkText (chunk.go:260-298) flushes on every heading-path change, so 10010+ distinct headings yield more than MaxChunks pieces. Not run.

Ledger 4.json F3 is resolved by documentation, which was one of the remedies that finding offered: extract.go:224-225 says a shallow scan leaves out subdirectories without a Skip and that Recursive takes them in.
